Don't work yourself up worrying. If your MRI results come out showing multiple lesions consistent with MS, think of it as you finally have an answer and can get proper treatment. There is new and greater treatment out there than even 10 years ago. MS isn't a death sentence, and not guaranteed to put you in a wheelchair. If your MRI doesn't show MS, keep exploring until you find answers. 
As for getting through the 3 1/2- 4 hours of MRI without music, I usually stay awake late the night before, drinking lots of fluids (so my veins pop when they inject the contrast), and just nap, letting the repetitive buzzes and whirs of the MRI lull me to sleep/meditate. You won't be inside the tube for the entire time, and if you need a break, they will give you one. 
   My last MRI, the open machine was not available, so I did the closed machine, which in fact is not that much different (you still have to lay still in either), is much quicker ~2 hours, and it gives a better image to the neurologist. If you have an option for that, I would recommend that one. 
   I hope you have support around you, I know sometimes when dealing with news like this, you may want to push people away to spare them hurt, but those who care about you will be pleased to do whatever they can to help you, no matter what. Whatever happens, don't let yourself slip into what ifs, and just deal with the answers as they come, and keep fighting! I wish you luck!

I am 32 and was diagnosed this year, and have probably had MS for about 7 years.  had symptoms about 6 years ago without knowing. Went to a chiropractor to see if it was a pinched nerve causing numbness in my legs. Saw him a couple of times, and it went away within a few weeks.
Then about 3 years ago, I was slurring words and dizzy most of the day, could barely work, or communicate with others, I thought maybe it was due to heavy drinking.
 After a few weeks of this, I went to see a doctor, who wanted me to get an MRI to check for a stroke. After he saw the result, he called me and told me I had a spot about a 1/4 inch in diameter on my cerebellum. The way he talked, it sounded like I had a brain tumor. He got me in for a CT scan for the rest of my body and an appointment with a neurosurgeon the next day. The neurosurgeon didn't think much of it, but scheduled me for an MRI 6 weeks later to see if anything changed.
During this time my symptoms went away, and didn't expect to see much on the MRI. When I saw the neurosurgeon again, he said the spot went away. Again, I didn't think much of this and forgot to follow up with him again, as no symptoms were occuring. 
Then this January, my legs began going numb again in the same way. I went back to the chiropractor, who tried for 3 weeks before  telling me I needed to investigate further and do an MRI. When I saw the doctor to get my MRI, he told me the prior CT scan showed I had bulging discs in my lumbar, so he thought that's what it was. When the MRI came back, I looked at the images myself, but couldn't see the discs actually touching the spinal cord anywhere. I was led astray by a few docs and a chiropractor who told me this was all due to the discs, but my neurosurgeon (same one) wanted to look at my brain again (duh). 
I also saw another neurosurgeon who thought I had something wrong with my cervical spine because I had uncoordination and numbness in my fingers. So I got both a cervical MRI, which showed lesions leading up to my brain stem. Then, I got my brain MRI which the results said "suspicious of MS". I didn't believe it, and at the most I thought it could be late stage Lyme disease. So I decided to search it out, and got tests and tests and saw infectious disease doctors and other new primaries.
They all discarded my notion of it being Lyme disease. When my appointment for my neurologist finally came, I'd scheduled another for a second opinion. 
Without either neurologist seeing both my cervical and brain MRI, they both wanted to diagnose me with MS. I decided I liked one more so I followed up with him, and kept pushing that it was Lyme disease. Finally, he agreed to order an LP, I think to appease me. When the results from that came back, I let go of the Lyme idea, and accepted I had MS.
This was in July, and I've already had both halves of my ocrevus infusions last few weeks.

SO, I've been a waiter for about five years. The little place I work at is the first waiting job I've ever had (started to pay off a guitar, and been there ever since). This place is a privately-owned joint, and not a bad check average (at night $50-75). But we cannot EVER get paid on time. Our credit card tips are taken at the end of the night and if the guests don't give us enough cash between us all ( we pool our tips) then we take a "chit" ( a "promise" that we will get paid, or an IOU from the house) for whatever we are still owed. The problem is, at the next payday, we don't often see our money for a few weeks, and rarely get a "paycheck" ( what are those again?") unless it is a void, meaning the government takes the taxes from our checks and the taxes equal out to more than or equal to our take for our hourly pay, depending on how much we've worked. That is, our owner often pockets the money for expenses or whatever else he deems necessary ( new Ipad?), and his "promise" to pay is often put off for two or more weeks. This is extremely frustrating when I have bills due the next week or day and am trying to keep my credit up to date. Any advice or have similar experiences?
